title: Audit Edge-Case Retention and Forensic Indexing Guidelines
author: Aisha Patel
summary: Guidelines for handling retention and indexing of audit data for edge cases (ephemeral credentials, cross-border incidents, model-serving failures). Defines triggers, retention overrides, forensic indexing schema, example queries, roles and handoff procedures to ensure evidence readiness for compliance and incident response.
content:
Purpose
This page defines special-case retention policies and forensic indexing requirements for audit data that fall outside our standard retention lifecycle. It focuses on scenarios that need accelerated capture, extended retention, or cross-jurisdictional packaging: credential leaks, model exfiltration attempts, emergency legal holds, and cross-border data residency incidents. The guidance aligns with corporate compliance obligations, incident response needs, and RBAC evidence requirements.

Scope
- Log sources covered: authentication events (AuthN), authorization/entitlement changes (AuthZ), system audit events (Kubernetes, service mesh), inference request traces (model-serving), storage access logs, and privileged session recordings.
- Storage systems: Elasticsearch (hot/warm), S3 immutable buckets, Kafka persistent topics, and WORM archive where required.
- Applies to hosted, dedicated, and private deployments; call out private deployments where customer-managed retention overrides exist.

Owner and Roles
- Evidence Custodian (primary): Security Forensics (security@redwood.com). Responsible for retention overrides and evidence packaging.
- Audit Owner: Observability Platform team. Maintains ingestion pipelines and indexing mapping.
- Compliance Liaison: Legal–Privacy. Authorizes cross-border evidence exports.
- Incident Commander: Person who opens the security incident. Triggers emergency retention flows.

Edge-Case Triggers (when to apply these guidelines)
1) Credential or secret compromise involving service or customer keys.
2) Confirmed or suspected model exfiltration (unexpected outbound data patterns, large prefix leaks).
3) Cross-border data residency concerns where logs indicate inference inputs/outputs crossing jurisdictions.
4) Privileged user session anomalies or suspicious role escalations.
5) External request from law enforcement or regulator needing preservation.

Immediate Actions (first 60 minutes)
1) Incident Commander declares retention hold and tags the incident in PagerDuty/incident tracker.
2) Evidence Custodian executes "preserve" command to switch ingestion to full-fidelity capture (no sampling) for affected services. Example CLI (obsctl):
   - obsctl retention hold --incident INC-12345 --services auth,model-serving --duration 90d --reason "credential-compromise"
3) Snapshot live KV-caches and model input buffers to immutable S3 bucket with access logging enabled.
   - aws s3 cp s3://redwood-ephemeral-snapshots/INC-12345/ --recursive --acl bucket-owner-full-control
4) Increase audit verbosity for involved components and mark related streams as "forensic" in Kafka to prevent TTL cleanup.

Preservation Policies and Durations
- Default production audit retention: 90 days hot, 365 days warm, archive to WORM after 365 days (see standard runbook).
- Edge-case retention overrides (applied per incident):
  - High-severity credential compromise: 2 years (forensic index), 7 years archive hold if requested by Legal.
  - Model exfiltration incident: retain request/response traces and model outputs for 3 years in immutable archive.
  - Cross-border legal hold: governed by Legal order; minimum retention 6 months unless restricted by local law.
- Temporary overrides must include expiration: every override requires an explicit auto-expiry or manual lift.

Forensic Indexing Schema (minimum fields)
All forensic-indexed events MUST include the following top-level indexed fields to support fast triage and evidence queries:
- event_id (UUID)
- incident_id (INC-XXXX)
- source_service (auth, model-serving, kv-store, s3, kube-audit)
- timestamp_utc (ISO8601)
- actor_principal (user/service id)
- actor_role (RBAC role at time of event)
- resource_path (canonical resource identifier)
- action (authenticate, assume_role, generate, ingest, export, train_request)
- request_id (correlates across traces)
- geo_country (derived from IP)
- retention_tier (forensic/hot/warm/archive)
- snapshot_ref (S3 path or object id)
- proof_of_integrity (sha256 hex)
- legal_hold (true/false)

Indexing best practices
- Use a dedicated forensic index prefix: forensic-YYYY-MM to ease retention and snapshot operations.
- Tag events with incident_id as soon as preservation is declared to avoid splicing evidence across indices.
- Maintain an append-only mapping of request_id -> request_shard to accelerate retrieval.
- Store checksums for any archived bundle and log checksum generation event.

Query Templates (examples)
- Find all escalations by a principal in a 24h window:
  ES query: {"query":{"bool":{"must":[{"term":{"actor_principal":"svc-data-processor"}},{"range":{"timestamp_utc":{"gte":"2027-01-02T00:00:00Z","lte":"2027-01-03T00:00:00Z"}}},{"term":{"action":"assume_role"}}]}}}
- Retrieve all model-serving traces with large outbound payloads:
  kql: source_service: model-serving AND response_bytes > 1048576 AND incident_id: *

Retention Matrix (summary)
| Event type | Default hot | Default warm | Forensic override | Archive action | Owner |
|-----------|-------------:|--------------:|------------------:|---------------|-------|
| AuthN success/failure | 30d | 365d | 2y | copy to WORM if legal_hold | Observability Platform |
| AuthZ changes (role binds) | 365d | 3y | 3y | WORM | IAM team |
| Model request/response traces | 14d | 90d | 3y | WORM for exfiltration incidents | Runtime team / Security Forensics |
| Privileged session recordings | 90d | 1y | 2y | WORM (if legal_hold) | SRE / Security Forensics |

(Notes: WORM = write-once-read-many immutable archive. Table is a quick reference; specific incidents may require Legal ordering.)

Cross-border and Data Residency Considerations
- When forensic capture would result in logs leaving a customer or user jurisdiction, obtain an expedited legal review. Do not export PII-containing logs without documented legal basis.
- For private deployments where customer controls retention, the Evidence Custodian must issue a formal preservation request to the customer point-of-contact and document responses in the incident record.
- Use geo-tagged indices to enable queries constrained to a jurisdiction — e.g., forensic-eu-2027-01.

RBAC and Evidence Chain Requirements
- All actions that initiate retention or snapshot extraction must be performed by RBAC principals with the role evidence_custodian or incident_commander.
- Every retention override must be logged as an auditable event with the following: who, what, why, duration, and approval token (if Legal required).
- Privileged approvals use just-in-time elevation with timebound authorization; record the elevation period as part of the event.

Evidence Packaging and Handoff Procedure (numbered runbook)
1) Evidence Custodian collects index identifiers and S3 snapshot_refs.
2) Verify integrity: compute sha256 on archive bundles and compare against logged proof_of_integrity.
3) Generate a human-readable manifest that includes legal_hold status, chain_of_custody entries, and a redaction plan for PII if required.
4) Package into immutable archive and replicate to a jurisdictionally appropriate WORM bucket. Example S3 object path: s3://redwood-evidence/INC-12345/forensics-bundle-2027-02-10.tar.gz
5) Create Evidence Ticket in case management system with links to manifest, checksums, and query templates for investigators.
6) Notify Legal and Compliance with a secure binding message (PGP-signed) and record the notification event id on the incident timeline.

Lift and Audit of Overrides
- Overrides auto-expire if not explicitly extended. A weekly audit job produces a report of active forensic indices and retention overrides and sends to Compliance Liaison.
- To lift an override: Evidence Custodian issues obsctl retention lift --incident INC-12345 --auth <approval_token>. All lifts are audited.

Reporting and KPIs
- Mean Time to Preservation (MTTP): target <= 30 minutes for declared incidents.
- Preservation completeness: >= 99% of relevant streams captured within retention window.
- Audit accuracy: zero mismatches between manifest checksums and stored bundles.

Example forensic JSON export (manifest entry)
{"event_id": "4f8f9a1c-...","incident_id": "INC-12345","source_service": "model-serving","timestamp_utc": "2027-02-10T17:14:22Z","actor_principal": "svc-feature-ingest","resource_path": "/models/ret-v2/predict","snapshot_ref": "s3://redwood-ephemeral-snapshots/INC-12345/trace-0001.json.gz","proof_of_integrity": "sha256:abc..."}

Exceptions and Risk Appetite
- Low-probability, high-impact events (e.g., mass model exfiltration) should default to more conservative retention (longer and geographic replication).
- Root-level decisions (extend past 7 years) require sign-off from Head of Security and Vice President, Legal.

Operational Playbook Integrations
- Integrate this guidance into incident runbooks used by oncall: include a step to contact Evidence Custodian in every incident with potential data leakage or privileged access anomalies.
- Observability Platform must provide a one-click retention-hold toggle in the incident UI that creates the incident_id and tags streams automatically.

Appendix A: Example obsctl commands
- Hold retention: obsctl retention hold --incident INC-12345 --services auth,model-serving --duration 365d --reason "suspected-exfiltration"
- Lift retention: obsctl retention lift --incident INC-12345 --auth-token XABCD1234
- Export manifest: obsctl export manifest --incident INC-12345 --output /tmp/INC-12345-manifest.json

Appendix B: Evidence checklist (quick)
- [ ] Incident declared and incident_id set
- [ ] Forensic capture toggled (no sampling)
- [ ] Snapshots copied to immutable storage with access logging enabled
- [ ] Checksums generated and logged
- [ ] Legal notified (if cross-border or PII involved)
- [ ] Manifest attached to evidence ticket

References
- Event schema contract: /confluence/security-and-compliance/audit-logging/event-schema-contract-and-retention-runbook-2025
- Forensic preservation playbook: /confluence/security-and-compliance/incident-response-security/forensic-log-preservation-and-legal-hold-playbook-2025
